q: The Bharatanatyam, with the araimandi and the adavu, is:
options: It is the folk dance of the Punjab
It is the classical dance of the Tamil temples with the araimandi and the adavu and the jati
It is the dance of Kerala
It is the dance of Odisha
explanation: The Bharatanatyam, the classical dance of the Tamil country, is marked by the araimandi, the adavu and the jati and the ashtami and the araimandi of the older temple tradition.

q: Rukmini Devi Arundale is best known for:
options: She founded the Kalakshetra in 1936 and she revived the Bharatanatyam
She was a noted singer of the Carnatic music
She was the founder of the Kalakshetra in 1948
She was a disciple of the Pandanallur Meenakshi Sundaram Pillai
explanation: The Rukmini Devi Arundale founded the Kalakshetra in Madras in 1936 and she was largely responsible for the revival of the Bharatanatyam on the stage.

q: The Kathak dance form developed in the:
options: It developed in the caves of Ellora
It developed in the royal courts of Mysore
It developed in the courts of Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras with the spins and the abhinaya
It developed in the temples of Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Kathak developed in the courts of Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras with the spins of the Delhi gharana, the vocabulary of the Lucknow gharana and the abhinaya of the Jaipur gharana.

q: The Kathakali, with the chuvanna thaadi and the elaborate make-up, is:
options: It is a martial dance of the Punjab
It is the classical dance-drama of Kerala with the elaborate make-up and the chuvanna thaadi
It is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu
It is the dance of Rajasthan
explanation: The Kathakali of Kerala combines the acting, the dance, the music and the costume with the elaborate make-up in which the chuvanna thaadi marks the demonic roles.

q: The Koodiyattam is:
options: Is the folk theatre of Karnataka
Is the dance of Odisha
Is a modern theatre form
Is the ancient Sanskrit theatre of Kerala and it is the only theatre form from the classical period still in existence
explanation: The Koodiyattam or the Kutiyattam, in which the performers speak in Sanskrit, is the only surviving theatre form from the classical period and it is inscribed on the UNESCO list.

q: The Mohiniyattam is:
options: It is the dance of Odisha
It is the folk dance of the Punjab
Is the classical dance of Kerala with the lasya and the grace and it is called the dance of the enchantress
It is the dance of Tamil Nadu
explanation: The Mohiniyattam, the lasya and the most beautiful of the classical dances, is the dance of the enchantress and it is associated with the stories of the Krishna.

q: Which of the following statements about the Odissi dance is correct?
options: Is the classical dance of Odisha with the tribhanga and the temple of the Jagannath at Puri
It is the dance of Kerala
It is the dance of Tamil Nadu
It is a folk dance of the Punjab
explanation: The Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha with the characteristic tribhanga and the Lasya and the Bhanga styles and it is the temple dance of the Jagannath at Puri.

q: The Manipuri dance is:
options: It is a temple dance of the south
Is the classical dance of Manipur with the Ras Lila and it was given the classical status in 1974
It is the dance of Kerala
It is the dance of the Rajputs
explanation: The Manipuri, with the Ras Lila of the Vaishnava tradition, was given the status of a classical dance in 1974 and it is the only classical dance of the North-East.

q: Which of the following statements about the Sattriya dance is correct?
options: It is the dance of Manipur
It is the folk dance of the Punjab
It is a temple dance of Kerala
Is the neo-Vaishnava dance of Assam codified by the Srimanta Sankardeva and it was recognised in 2000
explanation: The Sattriya, the neo-Vaishnava dance of Assam and Manipur codified by the Srimanta Sankardeva in the sixteenth century, was given the classical status in 2000.

q: Which of the following statements about the Chhau dance is correct?
options: It is the dance of Kerala
It is a martial dance of the Rajputs
It is the folk dance of the Punjab
Is the masked dance of the Seraikella, the Purulia and the Mayurbhanj and the Seraikella was given the classical status in 2010
explanation: The Chhau is a semi-classical dance from the Seraikella, the Purulia and the Mayurbhanj regions and the Seraikella Chhau was given the classical status in 2010.

q: Which of the following statements about the Gotipua dance is correct?
options: It is the dance of Kerala
Is the dramatic folk dance of the Mayurbhanj in Odisha which enacts the Puranic stories
It is the masked dance of the Seraikella
It is the classical dance of Manipur
explanation: The Gotipua is a dramatic folk dance of the Mayurbhanj region of Odisha in which the dancers enact the episodes from the Puranas and the Indian mythology.

q: The Ghoomar dance is:
options: It is a devotional dance of the Braj
It is a temple dance of Tamil Nadu
Is a folk dance of Rajasthan performed by the Bhil women
It is a Punjabi harvest dance
explanation: The Ghoomar is a folk dance of Rajasthan in which the women of the Bhil and the Garasia communities perform it in a circle with the clapping.

q: Which of the following statements about the Garba dance is correct?
options: Is the folk dance of Gujarat played during the Navratri
It is the dance of the Kerala temples
It is a martial dance of the Rajputs
It is the dance of the Devadasis
explanation: The Garba and the Dandiya are the community folk dances of Gujarat and they are played during the nine nights of the Navratri with the garba and the dandiya.

q: Which of the following statements about the Lavani dance is correct?
options: It is the dance of the Garhwal
It is a devotional dance of the temple
It is the folk dance of the Khasi hills
Is the folk dance of Maharashtra sung in a Marathi dialect
explanation: The Lavani of Maharashtra is a long narrative ballad of the wandering poet and the shepherd communities and it is sung in a Marathi dialect.

q: The 'Kummattikali' is:
options: A temple dance of Tamil Nadu
A theatre of the Devadasis
A folk theatre of Kerala performed on the fifth day of the Malayalam month of Meenam
A folk dance of the Punjab
explanation: The Kummattikali is a folk theatre of Kerala performed on the fifth day of the Malayalam month of Meenam with the vigorous singing and the drumming and the make-up.

q: The 'Yakshagana' of Karnataka:
options: Is the dance-drama with the elaborate headgear and the face painting and the vigorous chorus
It is a folk theatre of Kerala
It is a devotional theatre of the Bhakti movement
It is the theatre of the Marathas
explanation: The Yakshagana of coastal Karnataka and north Kerala is a dance-drama with the elaborate headgear, the face painting, the singing of the chorus and the vigorous acting.

q: The Badagutittu is:
options: the folk theatre of the Punjab
the closely related folk theatre of the coastal Karnataka
a temple dance of Tamil Nadu
the dance of the Pattachitra
explanation: The Badagutittu, with its simpler costume and the use of the stringed instruments, is the closely related folk theatre of the coastal Karnataka.

q: The 'Ankiya Naat' was codifed by:
options: Chandideva
Srimanta Sankardeva
Sankardeva's disciple
Madhavdeva
explanation: The Ankiya Naat, the Vaishnava neo-Vaishnavite musical play, was codified by the Srimanta Sankardeva and the Madhavdeva and the Chandideva followed him.

q: The 'Ramlila' of Ramnagar:
options: It is the opera of the Tamil Nadu
It is a ritual dance of the tribal Odisha
Is the traditional performance of the Ramayana with the masks and it was declared a UNESCO masterpiece in 2003
It is a folk theatre of the Punjab
explanation: The Ramlila of Ramnagar in Varanasi, performed with the wooden masks and the traditional style, was proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage by UNESCO in 2003.

q: The 'Nautanki' is:
options: A ritual dance of the south
A musical form of the Punjab
A painting style of the Rajputs
A folk theatre of northern India, especially of Awadh
explanation: The Nautanki, which evolved from the sung narration, is a folk theatre of the northern India and it is the most popular in the Awadh region of Uttar Pradesh.

q: Which of the following statements about the Tamasha folk theatre is correct?
options: Is the folk theatre of Maharashtra and the Bhavai is of Gujarat
It is the theatre of the Punjab
It is the temple theatre of Kerala
It is a ritual of the tribal Odisha
explanation: The Tamasha is the folk theatre of Maharashtra and the Bhavai of Gujarat, and both are the sung and the danced forms with the improvisation.

q: Which of the following statements about the IPTA is correct?
options: It was founded in 1930 in Calcutta
It was founded by the Prithvi Theatre
It was a commercial theatre
Was the progressive theatre movement founded in 1943 in Bombay
explanation: The Indian People's Theatre Association, founded in Bombay in 1943, was the most significant of the progressive theatre movements of India and it staged the plays of the Bhupen Hazarika.

q: Habib Tanvir is best known for:
options: He was a disciple of the Ebrahim Alkazi
He founded the Naya Theatre in 1959 and the Charandas was his most celebrated production
He founded the Prithvi Theatre
He founded the IPTA
explanation: The Habib Tanvir founded the Naya Theatre in 1959 and the Charandas, with its rustic setting of the village, was his most celebrated production.

q: The Badal Sircar is:
options: He founded the IPTA
He was a disciple of the B.V. Karanth
He founded the Third Theatre in Calcutta in 1970 and the street theatre for the common people
He founded the Naya Theatre
explanation: The Badal Sircar founded the Third Theatre in Calcutta in 1970 and his street plays brought the theatre to the common people in the rural Bengal.

q: Ebrahim Alkazi was:
options: the pioneer of the modern Indian theatre and he directed the Darpana and the Theatre Unit of the NSD
a painter
a film director
a poet
explanation: The Ebrahim Alkazi, a disciple of the Abdur Rehman and the Kutubuddin Shaikh, was the pioneer of the modern Indian theatre and he directed the Darpana and the Theatre Unit of the National School of Drama.

q: The National School of Drama of the India:
options: set up in 1975
in the Mumbai
set up by the Badal Sircar
set up in 1959 in New Delhi
explanation: The National School of Drama was set up in 1959 in New Delhi and it became the foremost institution of the theatre training in India.

q: The 'Raja Harishchandra' of 1913:
options: Was the first Indian film with an actress
Was the first documentary
Was the first Indian feature film made by the Dadasaheb Phalke
Was the first Indian talkie
explanation: The Raja Harishchandra of 1913, made by the Dadasaheb Phalke, was the first Indian feature film and the Phalke is known as the father of Indian cinema.

q: The 'Alam Ara' of 1931:
options: Was the first Indian documentary
Was the first Indian talkie film and it was directed by the Ardeshir Irani
Was the first Indian silent feature
Was the first colour film
explanation: The Alam Ara, directed by the Ardeshir Irani and released in 1931, was the first Indian talkie film and it was a commercial success.

q: The 'Kisan Kanya' of 1937:
options: Was the first Indian colour film and it was made by the Imperial Films
Was the first Indian talkie
Was the first Indian documentary
Was the first Indian animation
explanation: The Kisan Kanya of 1937, made by the Imperial Films, was the first Indian colour film and the first Indian film to be screened at the Cannes film festival.

q: The 'Pather Panchali' of 1955:
options: Won the Golden Bear at Berlin
Was the first film of the Parallel Cinema
Was a documentary
Won the Best Feature Film and the Best Cinematography at the first National Film Awards
explanation: The Pather Panchali of the Satyajit Ray won the Best Feature Film and the Best Cinematography awards at the inaugural National Film Awards of 1956 and it was based on the novel of the Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay.

q: The 'Apu Trilogy' of the Satyajit Ray:
options: Consists of the Pather Panchali, the Aparajito and the Apur Sansar
Consists of the Charulata and the Pratidwandi and the Ganashatru
Consists of the Mahanagar and the Charulata and the Shatranj
Consists of the Goopy Gyne and the Bagha Jatin and the Hirak Rajar Deshe
explanation: The Apu Trilogy consists of the Pather Panchali, the Aparajito and the Apur Sansar and the third part won the Golden Lion at the Venice film festival in 1959.

q: The 'Golden Bear' of the Berlin film festival was won by:
options: The Neecha Nagar
The Nagarik
The Pather Panchali
The Apur Sansar
explanation: The Pather Panchali won the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival in 1956 and the Apur Sansar won the Golden Lion at Venice in 1959.

q: The 'Neecha Nagar' of 1946:
options: Was the first documentary
Was the first Indian film to win the Grand Prix at the Cannes film festival
Was the first Indian talkie
Was the first Indian colour film
explanation: The Neecha Nagar of 1946, made by the Chetan Anand, was the first Indian film to win the Grand Prix at the Cannes film festival.

q: The 'Dadasaheb Phalke Award' was instituted in:
explanation: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the highest Indian award in cinema, was instituted in 1969 and it is presented by the President of India.

q: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was:
options: a pioneer of the Indian theatre and the founder of the Ballygunge theatre
a painter
the father of the Indian cinema
a musician
explanation: The Raja Ram Mohan Roy, a pioneer of the Indian theatre and the founder of the Ballygunge theatre, was the leading figure of the Bengali theatre of the nineteenth century.

q: Girish Karnad is best known as:
options: He directed the first Hindi talkie
He wrote the Tughlaq and the Kaagaz Te Patte and the Tabbal and the Chowka Bage
He wrote the Naya Theatre plays
He founded the IPTA
explanation: The Girish Karnad, a doyen of the Indian theatre, wrote the Tughlaq, the Kaagaz Te Patte, the Tabbal and the Chowka Bage and he won the Jnanpith in 1998.

q: Guru Dutt is best known for directing:
options: He directed the Aadmi Aur Aurat
He directed the first talkie
He was the father of the Indian parallel cinema
He directed the Pyaasa and the Sahib Bibi Aur Ghulam and he was a great actor of the golden age
explanation: The Guru Dutt, a legendary actor of the golden age of the Hindi cinema, directed the Pyaasa and the Sahib Bibi Aur Ghulam and he was the husband of the Geeta Dutt.

q: Bimal Roy is best known for directing:
options: He directed the Pyaasa
He directed the Aadmi Aur Aurat
He was a music director
He directed the Mother India and the Do Bigha Zamin and the Devdas
explanation: The Bimal Roy, often called the Greta Garbo of Indian cinema, directed the Mother India, the Do Bigha Zamin and the Devdas and he won the Best Director at Cannes for the Mother India.

q: Satyajit Ray is best known for:
options: He was a disciple of the Ritwik Ghatak
He composed the music of the Goopy Gyne, the Bagha Jatin and the Hirak Rajar Deshe and he won the Oscar for the Lifetime Achievement
He composed the music of the Mother India
He was the founder of the Film and Television Institute
explanation: The Satyajit Ray composed the music of his films like the Goopy Gyne, the Bagha Jatin and the Hirak Rajar Deshe and he received the honorary Academy Award in 1992.

q: Bhupen Hazarika was:
options: the director of the Pather Panchali
the founder of the Assamese cinema
the father of the Indian music and the film score of the Garm Hava
the founder of the Sangeet Natak Akademi
explanation: The Bhupen Hazarika is called the father of the Indian music and he composed the music of the Garm Hava and the Kal Aaj Aur Kal and he received the Bharat Ratna.

q: R.D. Burman is best known as:
options: He was a celebrated composer of the Hindi cinema and the son of the S.D. Burman
He was the director of the Mughal-e-Azam
He was a classical vocalist
He was a film producer
explanation: The R.D. Burman, the son of the S.D. Burman, was one of the most celebrated music directors of the Hindi cinema with the hits like the Mehbooba and the Chura Liya.

q: The Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer was:
options: a theatre pioneer
a leading Carnatic vocalist of the Pallava era
a Hindustani vocalist
a violinist
explanation: The Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer, a leading Carnatic vocalist of the 20th century, was the disciple of the Tiger of the East, the Chembai Vaidyanatha Bhagavatar.

q: The 'Gangubai Hangal' was a:
options: Hindustani vocalist of the Kirana gharana
Carnatic vocalist
A violinist
A composer of the film music
explanation: The Gangubai Hangal of the Kirana gharana was among the foremost Hindustani vocalists of the twentieth century and she received the Padma Bhushan in 2002.

q: The Hindustani music system is based on the:
options: The five shrutis and the twelve ragas
The seven notes and the four shrutis
The ten talas and the twelve vinas
The six taats of the Hindustani system and the melakarta in the Carnatic
explanation: The Hindustani system has the ten thaats of which the six are recognised, and the Carnatic has the seventy two melakarta ragas in the twelve vinas.

q: The Khayal in the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a percussion style
It is a devotional song of the Punjab
Is the principal vocal genre of the Hindustani music and it is the improvisational
Is the oldest vocal style
explanation: The khayal, the principal vocal genre of the Hindustani music, is the most frequently performed and it is based on the improvisation within the raga.

q: The Dhrupad of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is the Carnatic genre
It is a drum composition
It is a devotional genre of the Tamil Nadu
Is the oldest vocal genre of the Hindustani music and it is in the Dhrupad and the Dhama styles
explanation: The dhrupad, the oldest vocal genre of the Hindustani music, is sung in the Dhrupad and the Dhama styles and it is the ancestor of the khayal.

q: Which of the following statements about the Varnam of the Carnatic music is correct?
options: Is the improvised composition in the Carnatic music that precedes the main piece
Is a Hindustani genre
It is a percussion item
It is a temple ritual
explanation: The varnam, an improvised and an elaborate composition in the raga, precedes the main composition in a Carnatic concert and the most famous is the kritis of the Tyagaraja.

q: The Krits of the Carnatic music are:
options: Are the temple rituals
Are the compositions in the Carnatic music and the Trinity composed more than 4,000 of them
Are the drum compositions
Are the Hindustani thumris
explanation: The kritis, the composed pieces in the Carnatic music, number over 4,000 and the Tyagaraja, the Muthuswami Dikshitar and the Syama Sastri composed the bulk of them.

q: The 'Trinity' of the Carnatic music:
options: Balkavi and the Annamacharya
Venkatamakhin and the Sripandaraja
Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri
Purandara Dasa, Kanaka Dasa and Vyasatirtha
explanation: The Trinity of the Carnatic music is the Tyagaraja, the Muthuswami Dikshitar and the Syama Sastri of the eighteenth century, and the Annamacharya is called the father of the Carnatic music.

q: The 'Purandara Dasa' is known as the:
options: Father of the Vedic music
Father of the Carnatic music
Father of the Hindustani music
Father of the Bharatanatyam
explanation: The Purandara Dasa, a disciple of the Vyasaraja and a follower of the Vallabhacharya, is known as the father of the Carnatic music and he composed more than 4,000 songs.

q: The Bansuri of the Hindustani music is:
options: Is a percussion instrument
Is a bowed instrument
Is the bamboo flute of the Hindustani music
Is a string instrument
explanation: The bansuri, the bamboo flute, is the most common wind instrument of the Hindustani music and the shehnai is the double-reed one.

q: The Sarod of the Hindustani music is:
options: Is a fretless string instrument popularised by the Ravi Shankar
Is a drum of the Punjab
It is a vocal genre
It is a wind instrument
explanation: The sarod, a fretless string instrument with a wide bridge, was popularised by the Ravi Shankar and it is a principal instrument of the Hindustani music.

q: The Ghatam of the Carnatic music is:
options: Is a wind instrument
It is a bowed instrument
It is a vocal genre
Is the barrel-shaped percussion instrument of the Carnatic music
explanation: The ghatam, the clay pot with the drum stretched over it, is the principal percussion instrument of the Carnatic music along with the mridangam.

q: V.N. Bhatkhande is best known for:
options: He wrote the Natyashastra
He wrote the Sangita Ratnakari of the Carnatic
He wrote the Brihaddeshi
He wrote the Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati and the V.N. Bhatkhande’s Sangeet Ratnakari
explanation: The Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande wrote the Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati and the Sangeet Ratnakari, the two foundational works of the Hindustani music, and the S.N. Ratanjankar wrote the Sangita Ratnakari of the Carnatic.

q: The 'Sangita Ratnakari' was written by:
options: Purandara Dasa
S.N. Ratanjankar
V.N. Bhatkhande
Tyagaraja
explanation: The Sangita Ratnakari, the standard text of the Carnatic music, was written by the S.N. Ratanjankar and it is the companion of the Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati of the Bhatkhande.

q: The Bishnupur in Bengal is famous for its:
options: Is famous for the granite temples
Is famous for the wooden architecture of the Himalayan region
Is famous for the terracotta temples of the eighteenth century
Is famous for the white marble temples
explanation: The Bishnupur in the Manipur is famous for the terracotta temples of the eighteenth century with the figures of the Vaishnava deities and it was a centre of the Vaishnavite culture.

q: The Chettinad region of Tamil Nadu is famous for:
options: Is the region of the Tamil Nadu with the grand mansions of the Chettiar merchants
Is a region of the Telugu with the temples
Is a region of the Kerala with the backwaters
Is a region of the Punjab with the forts
explanation: The Chettinad, in the old Salem region of the Tamil Nadu, is famous for the grand mansions of the Chettiar merchants who traded with Southeast Asia.

q: The Vadutha style of architecture is:
options: Is the Kerala style of the architecture with the sloped roofs and the laterite and the wooden carvings
It is a Rajput style
It is a Mughal style
It is a Dravidian style
explanation: The Vadutha or the Kerala style uses the sloped roofs, the laterite, the wooden carvings and the murals and it is adapted to the heavy monsoon rainfall.

q: The Haveli houses of Rajasthan are:
options: Is the Chettiar house
It is the Mughal tomb
It is the temple of the Cholas
Is the Rajput mansion house with the courtyards and the frescoes
explanation: The haveli, the Rajput mansion house, has the inner courtyards, the frescoes and the jharokhas and the typical examples are in the Shekhawati of the Rajasthan and the Marwar.

q: The Shekhawati region of Rajasthan is known for:
options: It is the region of the marble work
Is the region of the Rajasthan with the havelis and the frescoes of the merchants
Is the region of the temple architecture
It is the region of the blue pottery
explanation: The Shekhawati region of the Rajasthan, with the havelis of the wealthy merchants, is the most painted region of the state and it is known as the open-air art gallery of Rajasthan.

q: The Sanganer near Jaipur is:
options: It is the terracotta of the Bishnupur
It is the marble of the Sikhs
Is the printing and the textile block printing centre of the Rajasthan near Jaipur
Is the temple architecture of the Rajputs
explanation: The Sanganer, near Jaipur, is the famous centre of the hand block printing and the bagru and the sanganeri prints are the pride of the Rajasthan.

q: The Bandhani craft is:
options: It is the weaving of the Kanjeevaram
Is the tie and dye technique of the Gujarat and the Rajasthan
It is the block print of the Sanganer
It is the embroidery of the Phulkari
explanation: The Bandhani, the tie and dye technique in which the tiny knots are tied before the dyeing, is the traditional craft of the Gujarat and the Rajasthan.

q: The 'Phulkari' of the Punjab:
options: It is a block print
It is a wood carving
Is a counted thread embroidery of the geometric patterns
Is a tie and dye technique
explanation: The Phulkari, literally the flower garden, is a counted thread embroidery of the Punjab with the geometric patterns worked in the long stitches.

q: The 'Chikankari' of Lucknow:
options: Is a tapestry of the Kashmir
It is a metal work of the Bidar
It is a wood carving of the Bihar
Is the shadow embroidery with the white thread on the muslin
explanation: The Chikankari, the shadow embroidery of Lucknow with the white thread on the fine muslin, is one of the oldest crafts of the Uttar Pradesh.

q: The shawls of the Kashmir are called the pashmina and the pashmina shawl is:
options: the GI product
called the bandhani
called the phulkari
called the kasuti
explanation: The shawls of the Kashmir are called the pashmina and the pashmina shawl of the Kashmir was the first Indian product to be given the GI tag in 2006-07.

q: The 'Toda embroidery' of the Nilgiris:
options: Is the block print
Uses the black and the white geometric motifs on the red or the black base
Uses the gold thread of the zari
Is the tie and dye
explanation: The Toda embroidery of the Nilgiri hills uses the black and the white geometric motifs, with the characteristic black squares and stripes, on a red or a black base.

q: The 'Kalamkari' of Andhra Pradesh:
options: Is the tie and dye
It is the embroidery of the Chettinad
It is the metal work of the Bidar
Is the hand painting or the block printing with the natural dyes
explanation: The Kalamkari of the Andhra Pradesh is the hand painting or the block printing of the cotton with the natural dyes, the indigo, the madder and the iron liquor.

q: The Banarasi silk is:
options: a wool of the Kashmir
a jute of the Bengal
a GI product of the Varanasi
a cotton of the Coimbatore
explanation: The Banarasi silk, with its zari brocade, is a GI tagged product of the Varanasi and the Kanjeevaram is the GI product of the Tamil Nadu.

q: The 'Channapatna toys' of Karnataka:
options: Are the GI tagged wooden toys painted with the natural colours
Are the GI tagged pottery
They are the GI tagged silk
They are the GI tagged jewellery
explanation: The Channapatna toys, made of the locally sourced wood and painted with the natural colours, were the first GI product of the Karnataka in 2009.

q: Which of the following statements about the Thanjavur painting is correct?
options: It is the tie and dye
It is the block print
Uses the gold foil on the teak panels with the gesso base
Uses the mirror work
explanation: The Thanjavur or the Tanjore painting of the Tamil Nadu uses the gold foil on the teak panels over a gesso base and it is also called the Tanjore painting.

q: The 'Bidriware' of Bidar:
options: Is the blackened alloy of zinc and copper with the silver inlay
Is the blue pottery of the Jaipur
It is the wooden toys of the Karnataka
It is the bronze of the Cholas
explanation: The Bidriware of the Bidar is the blackened alloy of the zinc and the copper with the silver inlay, and the craft is a GI product of the Karnataka.

q: The 'Khurja pottery' of Khurja:
options: Is the terracotta of the Bishnupur
It is the black pottery of the Khurja of the Assam
It is the pottery of the Pokkur
Is the glazed pottery of the Uttar Pradesh and it is a GI product
explanation: The Khurja pottery is the famous glazed pottery of the Khurja in the Uttar Pradesh and it is a GI product.

q: The 'Blue pottery' of Jaipur:
options: It is the blue glass
Is made of the quartz and the fuller earth with the cobalt oxide glaze
Is the blue and the white porcelain of the China
It is the blue dyed textile
explanation: The Jaipur blue pottery uses the quartz and the fuller earth instead of the kaolin and it is glazed with the cobalt oxide, and it is a GI product of the Rajasthan.

q: The 'Kullu shawls' of the Himachal:
options: They are the pashmina
Are the GI tagged handwoven woollen shawls with the bold geometric patterns
Are the GI tagged silk shawls
They are the cotton shawls
explanation: The Kullu shawls are the GI tagged handwoven woollen shawls of the Kullu in the Himachal Pradesh with the bold geometric patterns in the bright colours.

q: The Bagru and the Sanganeri are:
options: the block printing traditions of the Karnataka
of the Gujarat
the embroideries of the Punjab
the crafts of the Odisha
explanation: The Bagru and the Sanganeri are the two famous block printing traditions of the Rajasthan, not the Karnataka, and they are the pride of the Sanganer near Jaipur.

q: The Toda community of the Nilgiris is famous for its:
options: The Toda is a trading community of the Gujarat
The Toda is a fishing community of the Konkan
The Toda community of the Nilgiris is famous for the embroidery and the pashmina woollens
The Toda is a martial tribe of the Rajasthan
explanation: The Toda community of the Nilgiri hills is famous for its distinctive embroidery and for the pashmina woollen shawls that they weave.

q: The Kandangi and the Jamdani are:
options: the embroideries of the Punjab
the tile works
the metal crafts
the weaves of the Odisha and the Bengal
explanation: The Kandangi of the Odisha and the Jamdani of the Bengal are the fine muslin weaves on the pit loom and the Jamdani was given the GI tag.

q: The Pashmina wool is:
options: It is the silk of the Assam
It is the cotton of the Gujarat
It is the jute of the Bengal
The pashmina is the fine wool of the Changthangi goats of the Ladakh and the Kashmir
explanation: The pashmina is the fine wool of the Changthangi goats of the Ladakh and the Kashmir and the shawls of the region are among the finest in the world.

q: The Khadi is associated with the:
options: The Khadi was promoted by the Mahatma Gandhi as a symbol of the Swadeshi and the self sufficiency
It is a silk of the Bengal
It is a cotton of the Punjab
It is a wool of the Kashmir
explanation: The Khadi, the handwoven cloth of the handspun yarn, was promoted by the Mahatma Gandhi as a symbol of the Swadeshi and the self-sufficiency and it is now a protected GI product.

q: The 'Gamosa' of Assam:
options: It is the wool of the Kashmir
Is the traditional textile of the Assam worn with the white dhoti and the chador
It is a silk of the Varanasi
It is the cotton of the Coimbatore
explanation: The Gamosa, the traditional textile of the Assam, is worn with the white dhoti and the chador and it was given the GI tag in 2007.

q: The Kharvas of the Dal Lake are:
options: They are the ships of the Bengal
They are the canoes of the Assam
The Kharvas are the traditional houseboats of the Dal Lake of Srinagar
They are the boats of the Kerala backwaters
explanation: The Kharvas, the traditional houseboats of the Dal Lake of Srinagar, are the floating homes of the Kashmiri people and a few remain in use.

q: The Jali of the Mughal architecture is:
options: Is the perforated stone screen of the Mughal architecture
It is a textile of the Bengal
It is a musical instrument
It is a type of the carpet
explanation: The jali, the perforated stone or the wood screen, is a distinctive feature of the Mughal architecture and it lets in the light while preserving the privacy.

q: The 'Chhatri' of Rajasthan:
options: It is the enclosed courtyard
It is the vaulted chamber
It is the minaret
Is the small domed kiosk on the pillars of the Rajput architecture
explanation: The chhatri, the small domed kiosk on the pillars, is a distinctive feature of the Rajput architecture and it is placed on the corners of the courtyards and the terraces.

q: The 'Sarai' of the Mughal architecture:
options: It is the tomb
Is the open hall of the serais for the travellers and the merchants
It is the royal chamber
It is the mosque
explanation: The sarai, the open hall with the surrounding rooms, was the rest house of the Mughal serais and it provided the accommodation to the travellers and the merchants and the animals.

q: The Minaret of a mosque is:
options: It is the domed chamber
It is the tomb
Is the tower from which the muezzin calls the faithful to the prayer
It is the entrance gateway
explanation: The minaret, the tower of the mosque from which the muezzin calls the faithful to the prayer, is a distinctive element of the Islamic architecture in India.

q: The 'Iwan' of the Persian architecture:
options: It is the gateway
It is the dome
Is the vaulted hall open on one side of the courtyard
It is the minaret
explanation: The iwan is the vaulted hall open on one side of the courtyard and it is a hallmark of the Persian architecture that was adopted in the Mughal buildings.

q: The Rabat of the Deccan palaces is:
options: It is a garden pavilion
Is the residential quarters of the Qutb Shahi and the Adil Shahi palaces
It is a type of the minaret
It is a kind of the carpet
explanation: The rabat is the residential quarters of the Qutb Shahi and the Adil Shahi palaces and the Rabati Bagh of the Golconda is the finest of them.

q: The Ashurkhana of the Deccan is:
options: Is the royal congregation hall of the Qutb Shahi and the Adil Shahi palaces
It is a temple
It is a kitchen
It is a prison
explanation: The Ashurkhana, the royal congregation hall of the Qutb Shahi and the Adil Shahi palaces, was used for the prayer and it has the Persian style of the decoration.

q: The 'Tavil' of the Tamil Nadu:
options: Is a wind instrument
It is a string instrument
It is a clay vessel
Is a percussion instrument of the Carnatic music
explanation: The tavil, a large copper wind instrument, is used in the Carnatic music and it is played with the Venkatachalam and the Nattukara of the Tiruvallur tradition.

q: The 'Morsing' of the Carnatic music:
options: It is a string instrument
It is a clay drum
Is a percussion instrument of the South Indian tradition
Is a wind instrument of the north
explanation: The morsing is a percussion instrument of the South Indian tradition and the temple percussion of the Carnatic music includes the mridangam, the ghatam, the morsing, the kanjira and the tavil.

q: The Kanjira of the Carnatic music is:
options: Is a small percussion instrument of the Carnatic music
It is a wind instrument
It is a string instrument
It is a bell
explanation: The kanjira, a small clay or the metal drum, is a percussion instrument of the Carnatic music and it is held in one hand and struck with the other.

q: The Rudra veena of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a percussion instrument
It is a wind instrument
It is a vocal genre
Is a bowed string instrument of the Hindustani music
explanation: The Rudra veena, with its twenty-four frets, is a bowed string instrument of the Hindustani music and it is the ancestor of the modern violin.

q: The Sarangi of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a vocal genre
Is a bowed string instrument of the Hindustani music
It is a drum of the Punjab
It is a wind instrument
explanation: The sarangi, a three stringed bowed instrument with a skin-covered resonator, is the principal instrument of the Hindustani music for the imitation of the voice.

q: The Esraj of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a percussion instrument
It is a wind instrument
It is a vocal genre
Is a bowed string instrument of the Hindustani music
explanation: The esraj, with its hundred sympathetic strings, is a bowed string instrument of the Hindustani music and it is used for the vocal and the instrumental styles.

q: The Shehnai of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a string instrument
Is the double-reed wind instrument of the Hindustani music
It is a bowed instrument
It is a percussion instrument
explanation: The shehnai, the double-reed wind instrument, is a principal instrument of the Hindustani music and it is popularly known as the Indian oboe.

q: The Chaturang composition is:
options: Is the Carnatic composition in the praise of the Rama
It is a Hindustani genre
It is a percussion item
It is a temple ritual
explanation: The chaturang, the Carnatic composition in the praise of the Rama, is the most ancient of the compositions and it is followed by the varnam.

q: The 'Thumri' of the Hindustani music:
options: It is a drum composition
It is a Carnatic genre
Is a semi-classical genre with the romantic lyrics sung in the khamaj thaat
Is the oldest style
explanation: The thumri is a semi-classical genre of the Hindustani music with the romantic lyrics and it is sung in the khamaj thaat and it is the staple of the Banaras and the Lucknow gharana.

q: The Kafi of the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a percussion style
It is a temple song
Is a thaat of the Hindustani music and a genre of the semi-classical
It is a raga of the Carnatic
explanation: The kafi is one of the six recognised thaats of the Hindustani music and it is also a semi-classical genre with the romantic and the Sufi poetry.

q: The Patiala in the Hindustani music is:
options: It is a musical instrument
Is a gharana of the Hindustani music founded by the Ali Baksh and the Fateh Ali Khan
It is a Carnatic school
It is a poetry genre
explanation: The Patiala gharana was founded by the Ali Baksh and the Fateh Ali Khan and it is noted for its compositions in the dhrupad and the dhamar styles.

q: The 'Gwalior gharana' was founded by:
options: Ali Baksh and the Fateh Ali Khan
Abdul Karim Khan
Nawab Fateh Ali Khan
Hasan Khan
explanation: The Gwalior gharana was founded by the Hasan Khan, a descendant of the Tansen, and it is known for the intricate bandish and the sargam style.

q: The 'Nandalal Bose' was:
options: A disciple of the Abanindranath Tagore and the principal designer of the national flag
A disciple of the Gandhi
The founder of the Bombay Progressive Artists' Group
A disciple of the M.F. Husain
explanation: The Nandalal Bose, a disciple of the Abanindranath Tagore, was the principal designer of the national flag of India and he was the founder of the Kala Bhavana at the Santiniketan.

q: The 'Bengal school' of painting was founded by:
options: Abanindranath Tagore
Raja Ravi Varma
Nandalal Bose
Abanindranath and the Nandalal Bose
explanation: The Bengal school of painting was founded by the Abanindranath Tagore in the early twentieth century with the aim of reviving the Indian art tradition and it included the Nandalal Bose and the Ramkinkar Baij.

q: The 'Bombay Progressive Artists' Group' was formed in:
explanation: The Progressive Artists' Group was formed in Bombay in 1947 with the M.F. Husain, the F.N. Souza, the S.H. Raza, the K.H. Ara and the H.A. Gade and it challenged the academic realism.

q: The Raja Ravi Varma was:
options: He founded the Bengal school
He founded the Madras Art Movement
He was a disciple of the Abanindranath Tagore
He reformed the Indian art with the academic realism and the oil technique and he painted the Bharat Mata
explanation: The Raja Ravi Varma, a painter of the Kerala palace, reformed the Indian art with the academic realism and the oil technique and his Bharat Mata became a national icon.

q: The 'Amrita Sher-Gil' was:
options: A sculptor of the Chola period
A painter of the Rajput school
An Indian painter of the modern period who studied in Paris and is known for the self portraits
A painter of the Bengal school
explanation: The Amrita Sher-Gil, who studied in Paris, is one of the pioneers of the modern Indian painting and her self portraits are celebrated for the psychological depth.

q: The 'K.G. Subramanyan' was:
options: A painter of the Bengal school
A disciple of the Nandalal Bose
A painter of the Madhubani
A painter and a muralist of the modern India who was also a scholar of the Indian folk traditions
explanation: The K.G. Subramanyan, a painter, a muralist and a scholar of the Indian folk tradition and the epics, is one of the most important of the modern Indian painters.

q: The 'Ramkinkar Baij' was:
options: A painter of the Western Ghats
A painter of the Company style
A painter of the Bengal school who painted the Santhal life
A painter of the Madhubani
explanation: The Ramkinkar Baij, a leading painter of the Bengal school, is known for his depictions of the Santhal life and the rural Bengal and he was also a sculptor.

q: The 'Madras Movement' in art was led by:
options: The Amrita Sher-Gil
D.P. Roy Chowdhury and the K.C.S. Paniker
The M.F. Husain
The F.N. Souza
explanation: The Madras Art Movement was led by the D.P. Roy Chowdhury, the K.C.S. Paniker and the S. Dhanapal and it championed the modern and the indigenous traditions.

q: The 'Company painting' developed:
options: In the late eighteenth century for the European patrons
In the Vijayanagara period
In the Mughal period
In the Pala period
explanation: The Company painting developed in the late eighteenth and the early nineteenth centuries as the Indian artists worked for the European traders and the administrators.

q: The 'Rajput painting' schools:
options: Include only the Mughal
Include the Kangra and the Guler
Include only the Vijayanagara
Include the Mewar, the Bundi and the Kishangarh and the Kota
explanation: The Rajput schools include the Mewar, the Bundi, the Kishangarh, the Kota, the Jaipur, the Guler and the Kangra and they depict the courtly and the devotional themes.

q: The 'Mughal painting' reached its peak under:
options: Jahangir
Akbar
Shah Jahan
Aurangzeb
explanation: The Mughal painting reached its zenith under the Jahangir with the single figure portraits, the allegorical compositions and the calligraphic work and the Akbar favoured the narrative.

q: The paintings patronised by the Akbar are:
options: The Akbar preferred only the religious paintings
The Akbar preferred the narrative and the historical paintings with the Persian and the Indian elements
The Akbar preferred only the portraits
The Akbar did not patronise the painting
explanation: The Akbar, who was a great patron of the painting, preferred the narrative and the historical paintings with a synthesis of the Persian and the Indian elements, and the Hamzanama was his biggest commission.

q: The paintings patronised by the Shah Jahan are:
options: He was not a patron of the painting
He preferred the abstract
The Shah Jahan preferred the formal and the portraiture and the MUGHAL album was the model
The Shah Jahan preferred only the religious paintings
explanation: The Shah Jahan preferred the formal and the portraiture and his reign is considered the golden age of the Mughal art with the MUGHAL album as the model.

q: Kangra painting is:
options: a Rajput school of the fifteenth century
a Mughal school
a Company style
a Pahari school of the eighteenth century and the Amritotsava is its finest work
explanation: The Kangra painting is a Pahari school of the eighteenth century and the Amritotsava, the Darshan of the Lord, is its finest work.

q: The Rajput painting is known for the:
options: It depicts only the portraits
The Rajput painting depicts the courtly and the devotional themes with the Krishna legend
It depicts only the battles
It depicts only the hunting
explanation: The Rajput painting depicts the courtly and the devotional themes with the Krishna legend and the romantic love of the Radha and the Krishna.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the Kalighat temple of Calcutta is correct?
options: The temple of the Jagannath at Puri
The temple of the Minakshi at Madurai
The Kalighat temple of Calcutta in the nineteenth century
The Kalighat temple of Varanasi
explanation: The Kalighat painting developed in the nineteenth century around the Kalighat temple in Calcutta and it used the imported colours and the bold brushwork on the flat paper.

q: The 'Pattachitra' of Odisha and Bengal:
options: Is the cloth scroll painting tradition
It is the mural tradition of the Karnataka
It is the miniature of the Rajasthan
It is the rock cut of the Ajanta
explanation: The Pattachitra, the cloth scroll painting of the Odisha and the Bengal, was traditionally used as the temple curtain of the Jagannath at Puri and the Chitrakala is the mural tradition of the Karnataka.

q: The 'Madhubani painting' of Bihar:
options: Uses the bold geometric patterns with the double line borders and the natural dyes
It uses the gold foil
It is the miniature of the Rajasthan
It is the mural of the tribal Bhils
explanation: The Madhubani or the Mithila painting of the Bihar uses the bold geometric patterns, the double line borders and the natural dyes and it is practised mainly by the women.

q: The 'Warli painting' of Maharashtra:
options: It uses the gold foil
It is the miniature of the Rajputs
It is the mural of the Bhils
Uses the simple stick figures of the white on the mud brown background
explanation: The Warli painting of the Maharashtra uses the simple stick figures of the white pigment on the mud brown background and it depicts the daily life and the deities.

q: The Kalamkari of the Srikalahasti and the Machilipatnam is:
options: the embroidery of the Chettinad
the metal craft of the Bidar
the hand-painted and the block-printed cotton
the tie and dye
explanation: The Kalamkari of the Srikalahasti in the Andhra Pradesh and the Machilipatnam in the Telangana is the hand-painted and the block-printed cotton with the natural dyes.
